function_v0.doc:
Transfer the admin role to `new_admin` (current admin only). Deployment hands the role to
the governance timelock once every venue is registered, which is what puts `upgrade`,
`upgrade_positions`, `replace_venue` and the pause/emergency switches behind the timelock \xe2\x80\x94
governance classifies any unlisted method as Sensitive, so no per-setter code is needed
here. Without this the broker would be stuck on its deployer key for good: no handover, and
no rotation if it leaks.
function_v0.name: set_admin

function_v0.doc:
Bind a borrow venue to a *market* + collateral asset. `compound_token` is the pool's rate
identity (`PoolKey::compound_token` \xe2\x80\x94 the borrow-index-source instance), so one registration
covers every term traded on that market, and a pool can never route to another lending's
venue. Registering by debt token instead would collide across lendings, since the same
(debt, collateral) pair exists on all of them.

**Creation-only**: an already-registered pair is rejected, which is what lets governance
classify this as Deployer-tier and run it instantly \xe2\x80\x94 onboarding a venue happens during a
deploy and must not wait out a timelock. Repointing a pair that is already serving hedges is
a different act and lives on [`Self::replace_venue`], which stays Sensitive.
function_v0.name: set_venue

function_v0.doc: Repay up to `amount` of the hedge's venue debt; excess is refunded to the caller.\nReturns the amount actually repaid.
function_v0.name: repay_debt

function_v0.doc:
Set the pause flag (admin only). The `bool` shape is what the governance guardian's
`guardian_pause(target, paused)` invokes, so the broker is reachable by the same emergency
brake as the engine and LockYield; [`pause`](Self::pause) / [`unpause`](Self::unpause) are
the no-arg sugar over it.

Pausing the engine is not a substitute. It does stop the paths that touch CE margin \xe2\x80\x94 hedge
opens and [`deposit_margin`](Self::deposit_margin) \xe2\x80\x94 but
[`add_collateral`](Self::add_collateral) only
moves tokens into the *venue*, so an engine pause leaves users still funding a lending
market that may be exactly what is on fire. The engine brake is also protocol-wide: halting
LockYield too, to contain a venue incident, is the wrong blast radius.

Once [`enable_emergency`](Self::enable_emergency) has run, the pause can no longer be
lifted through either shape \xe2\x80\x94 emergency is irreversible and implies pause.
function_v0.name: set_paused

function_v0.doc:
Settle a matured hedge's IRS leg. The engine consumes the account's borrowed-underlying
margin first. If a loss exhausts it and the user later added venue-collateral margin, the
authenticated settler funds the residue and receives that fallback collateral through the
engine's auto-exchange. The venue leg is left untouched.

function_v0.name: add_collateral

function_v0.doc: Top up one of the hedge's CE margin balances. Opens fund it with borrowed underlying;\ncallers may later add any other engine-configured asset. The CE account remains isolated to\nthe pool underlying for position eligibility.
function_v0.name: deposit_margin

function_v0.doc:
Reduce the hedge's VT leg with a Fixed-Taker-direction swap.
Partial unwinds are fine (no notional-mismatch check), mirroring `unwindPosition`.

`variable_tokens` is how much of the **variable leg** to retire, in the pool's
term-start-anchored tokens \xe2\x80\x94 the unit `variable_token_balance` is stored in, so passing that
balance closes the leg out to exactly zero.

Tokens rather than notional because the token balance is the stable coordinate: it changes
only when the position is touched, while the notional that closes it grows with the index on
every ledger. A caller naming a notional off-chain is therefore always slightly short by the
time the transaction lands, and retrying against the residue retires `1 / (1 + accrued)` of
it each round \xe2\x80\x94 geometric, never reaching zero. The conversion happens on-chain in
[`notional_to_close`](xccy_vamm_interface::VammClient::notional_to_close), against the same
index this swap will use and floored so the swap's ceiling lands back on exactly this many
tokens.
function_v0.name: unwind_position

function_v0.doc:
Open (or grow) a borrow hedge. Returns the full [`OpenResult`], so a transaction
simulation reports the post-trade swap outputs, margin requirement and (when the
health read is requested) the venue position in one call.

`collateral_amount` of `collateral_asset` is supplied to the venue, `borrow_amount`
of the pool's underlying is borrowed against it. `margin_amount` of the borrowed
underlying is posted as CE margin backing a Variable-Taker swap over the full borrow; the
calculated opening trade fee is included in that margin, and whatever the venue delivered
beyond the margin is paid out to the caller.

The swap is sized on `borrow_amount` because that is the debt the market records, but the
payout is sized on what actually arrived: a market whose one-time borrow fee comes out of the
disbursement credits less than it debits. `VenueCreditedBelowMargin` if the delivery does
not cover the requested IRS margin. A `min_health_factor` above `1.0` WAD makes

function_v0.doc:
Leveraged open (port of `openLeveragedBorrowHedge`): flash-borrow `borrow_amount`
of the pool's underlying, sell it (plus any user deposit) for venue collateral
through the swap aggregator along `swap_xdr`, and land in the same end state as
`open_borrow_hedge` \xe2\x80\x94 collateral supplied, debt outstanding, margin posted, VT swap
open \xe2\x80\x94 without the user fronting all venue collateral. `margin_amount` is held back
from the flash-borrowed debt asset and posted to CE; it includes the opening trade fee.

`deposit_asset` must be the debt or the collateral asset: a collateral deposit raises the

where the quote is (a `StrategyPayload` serialized with `to_xdr`); the venue checks it names
that pair and carries at least `min_collateral_out`, so a bad route costs the caller a
reverted open and nothing else. `min_collateral_out` bounds swap slippage AND anchors the
venue's flash health c

(compound_token, collateral_asset) -> borrow venue (a `borrow-venue` manager:
`blend-borrow-venue` / `xoxno-borrow-venue`).

Keyed by the pool's *rate identity*, not by its debt token: the same (debt, collateral) pair
exists on every lending we support, so a token-keyed registry would let a hedge swap one
market's index while borrowing on another. `compound_token` is the borrow-index-source
instance, bound 1:1 to a (protocol, market), and it comes off the same `PoolKey` the IRS leg
trades \xe2\x80\x94 so the venue cannot drift from the pool. Collateral stays in the key because it is

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Venue-side position snapshot. Every field is a by-product of the single valuation pass
a health read already performs, so a snapshot costs no cross-contract calls beyond that
read; a venue that cannot produce a field in the same frame leaves it zero. Base values
are in the venue oracle's base units (the scale cancels out of `health`, so it is
venue-defined and only ratios of base values are portable); factors are the venue's
native risk weights in the venue's native scale (Blend: 7-decimal `c_factor`/`l_factor`;
Alula: bps `close_ltv`/`liability_factor`; XOXNO: not exposed, `0`).
udt_struct_v0.name: VenueSnapshot

walk them live, so without this ceiling an account can be grown past what its own exit paths
fit in one transaction and become un-liquidatable, un-settleable bad debt (see
[`crate::caps`]). Liquidations and the ESM's own book are exempt.
cases.name: PositionMaxReached

cases.doc: The caller is not the account owner (port of the EVM `_requireAuthorized` revert).
cases.name: Unauthorized

cases.doc: A trade reached a pool inside its `closing_window` \xe2\x80\x94 the stretch before `term_end` where\nrequired margin has shrunk with the term left to run. Liquidation, settlement, early\nsettlement and `apply_adl` are unaffected.
cases.name: PoolClosing

cases.doc:
`execute_early_settlement` was asked to open exposure rather than retire it \xe2\x80\x94 a delta that
grows the standing fixed leg, or one that overshoots it and flips the leg through zero onto
the other side. The ESM is an exit venue, the counterparty of last resort for the fixed tail
an unwind leaves behind, so it may only walk a pre-existing leg toward zero. A zero balance
admits no delta at all, which is what stops a position being created from nothing against
the ESM's inventory.
cases.name: EsmOpensExposure

cases.doc: The account selected for ADL is already below its liquidation threshold and must go through\nthe ordinary liquidation path instead.
cases.name: AdlCandidateLiquidatable

cases.doc: The candidate's actual post-unwind claim cannot cover the caller's minimum requested amount.
cases.name: AdlCoverBelowMinimum

cases.doc: A fee root publication did not advance the globally monotonic sequence.
cases.name: StaleFeeRoot

cases.doc: A user tried to sell a positive fixed claim to the ESM while this pool still has an\noutstanding ADL deficit. The claim remains available to cover that deficit; buying fixed\nto retire a negative leg is still allowed.
cases.name: EarlySettlementBlockedByAdl

udt_struct_v0.doc: Global wiring, set at construction (`vamm` set afterwards via `set_vamm`).
udt_struct_v0.name: Config

fields.doc: APR oracle \xe2\x80\x94 variable factor / settlement (Milestone B).
fields.name: apr_oracle

fields.doc: The Early Settlement Manager, queried for the discounted price in\n`execute_early_settlement` (set afterwards via `set_esm`).
fields.name: esm

fields.doc: Reflector price oracle \xe2\x80\x94 collateral valuation (Milestone B).
fields.name: price_oracle

fields.doc: The VAMM allowed to call `update_position_post_vamm_action`.
fields.name: vamm

udt_union_v0.doc: Why a fee was accrued. The backend uses this to distinguish a prepaid taker fee from an\nimmediately distributable liquidation-unwind fee without inferring intent from neighbouring\nevents.
udt_union_v0.name: FeeKind

udt_struct_v0.doc: The globally published fee-distribution root and its monotonic publication sequence.
udt_struct_v0.name: FeeRoot

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One LP/taker position's accounting (a trimmed `Position.Info`: most liquidation fields
omitted). `*_growth_inside_last` snapshot the per-unit-liquidity X128 accumulators; an LP
position's accrued balances are reconstructed from them in [`crate::growth`].

Two ledgers travel alongside the balances, both in the pool's term-start-anchored tokens \xe2\x80\x94 the
same unit as `variable_token_balance`, and **not** notionals despite what the per-pool caps are
configured in; those multiply by `1 + accrued` at the comparison ([`crate::caps`]).

`traded_tokens` is the position's **counted exposure**: its contribution to the pool's
[`OpenInterest`]. Every explicit trade moves it at full size, including one a range makes against
its own leg \xe2\x80\x94 that is not a netting, its counterparty is whoever holds liquidity at the current
tick. A range's *fills* are deliberately not counted; they arrive through growth-inside, and the
pool's variable legs sum to zero, so bounding the traded sides bounds the ranges implicitly. When
a range is b
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.doc: VAMM price matching the stored balances and growth baselines. The hook-safe valuation\nsweeps from this price, keeping the realized and hypothetical parts at one point in time.
fields.name: sqrt_price_at_last_sync

udt_struct_v0.doc: Aave-style per-asset collateral config.
udt_struct_v0.name: AssetConfig

fields.doc:
Max total margin (base units) the engine will hold of this asset across all accounts; `0`
disables it. Tracked as the sum of every account's balance \xe2\x80\x94 maintained inside
[`crate::account::apply_delta`], so a seizure or settlement auto-exchange gives its headroom
back the way a withdrawal does. Enforced entry-time on deposit only: lowering it blocks new
deposits but never forces a withdrawal, and internal credits (settlement, fees) move the
gauge but are never gated by it.
fields.name: deposit_max

fields.doc: Minimum collateral balance (base units) a user may hold of this asset; `0` disables it. After a\nuser deposit or withdrawal the balance must be `0` or `>= deposit_min` \xe2\x80\x94 dust collateral is\nun-liquidatable one asset at a time, so holding it (and letting it back margin) is barred.
fields.name: deposit_min

fields.doc:
The only account owner allowed to post this asset as margin; `None` leaves it open to anyone.

Set it to the LockYield broker to make the asset a **self-settling wrapper share**: it must
then carry a zero `auto_exchange_bonus` (enforced together with this field, so the pair can
never drift apart), which is exactly what lets matured settlement redeem it at par instead of
selling it to a settler at a discount ([`crate::settlement`]). That zero bonus is also why it
must be confined here \xe2\x80\x94 anywhere else it would be un-seizable collateral backing an
un-liquidatable position. Presence of this field is what arms the self-redeem.
fields.name: restricted_depositor

udt_struct_v0.doc: An element of an account's position list: the pool (by `pool_id`) and tick range.
udt_struct_v0.name: PositionKey

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A pool's **open interest** in variable-token base units: the two one-sided sums of every
position's `traded_tokens` (`variable_receiving` = the positive side, `variable_paying` = the
magnitude of the negative side).

Stored in tokens, compared in underlying: `notional_max` is configured in the underlying, so each
side is multiplied by `1 + accrued` at the check rather than at the booking \xe2\x80\x94 see
[`crate::caps`] for why only the token count is time-invariant. The two units coincide at
`term_start` and diverge from there.

Three properties make this the right quantity to cap, rather than the pool's net position or the
gross flow through it:

* **Per-position netting.** Each position contributes its *current* signed `traded_tokens`, so
a round trip (open then close, in one account) leaves no residue. Summing trade magnitudes
instead would let free wash trades ratchet the pool into its own cap.
* **Both sides, not the net.** An index-manipulation profit scales with the attacker's *own*
variable-receiving notional
udt_struct_v0.name: OpenInterest

udt_struct_v0.doc: A pool's [`WorstCaseVariableFactor`] together with the thresholds it implies \xe2\x80\x94 the points an\nLP's worst-case sweep is cut at ([`crate::lp_margin`]).
udt_struct_v0.name: PoolWorstCase

fields.doc: `factor`'s three rates as cut points, derived once when the envelope is written.
fields.name: cut_positive

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The full per-pool risk configuration written once, atomically, by `initialize_pool` \xe2\x80\x94 the
runtime "constructor" for a pool on the shared engine. The engine and VAMM are singletons that
host every pool, so a pool's params cannot live in a contract constructor; they are set when the
pool is added. The individual `set_*` setters mutate these afterwards (each a timelocked
governance op); `initialize_pool` writes them all on a not-yet-configured pool and rejects an
already-configured one. `notional_min`/`notional_max`/`protocol_fee_rate` of `0` disable those.
udt_struct_v0.name: PoolRiskConfig

fields.doc:
Seconds before `term_end` in which the pool stops accepting **trades**; `0` disables it.

Liquidation, settlement, early settlement and `apply_adl` keep working. Two reasons:

* The margin a position requires is proportional to the term it still has to run, so as
`term_end` approaches the notional a given deposit supports grows without bound. Such a
position is worth about nothing, but its *balances* are not, and they land in open
interest, ADL candidate selection and the deficit ledger all the same.
* ADL has only until `term_end` \xe2\x80\x94 the VAMM refuses its liquidation entrypoints once the term
is over \xe2\x80\x94 so a still book keeps the candidate its backend picked valid long enough to act
on.

Per-pool rather than global because it is a fraction of the tenor: an hour is nothing to a
one-year pool and 4% of a one-day one.
fields.name: closing_window

udt_struct_v0.doc: Per-asset risk parameters (WAD). An asset carries two: a `default` (cross-margin) path\nand an `isolated` path used when it is the account's `isolated_margin_token`.
udt_struct_v0.name: AssetRiskConfig

fields.doc: Auto-exchange / liquidation bonus (WAD): the discount a liquidator (seizure) or settler\n(settlement ADL exchange) receives on this collateral.
fields.name: auto_exchange_bonus

fields.doc: Liquidation threshold (WAD), `\xe2\x89\xa5 ltv`.
fields.name: liquidation_threshold

fields.doc: LTV (WAD). Margin gate: `\xce\xa3 amount\xc2\xb7price\xc2\xb7ltv \xe2\x89\xa5 obligation`.
fields.name: ltv

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Per-pool worst-case variable factor envelope (WAD annual rates) \xe2\x80\x94 bounds the unknown variable
leg when valuing a position.

`[positive_wad, negative_wad]` is the range the variable rate is expected to realize in:
`positive_wad` is the worst case for a position *receiving* variable (the rate collapses),
`negative_wad` the worst case for one *paying* it (the rate spikes).

`max_rate_wad` is the hard ceiling \xe2\x80\x94 the underlying venue's borrow APR at 100% utilization.
It is what the envelope widens to once a price path falsifies the envelope on that side: an
LP whose liquidity only gets consumed at fixed rates above `negative_wad` is, in the scenario
where that happens, holding a position the envelope never described, so its variable leg is
bounded by the ceiling instead. The mirror case \xe2\x80\x94 a path below `positive_wad` \xe2\x80\x94 widens the
receiving side down to zero. Only the side the path actually breached is widened.
udt_struct_v0.name: WorstCaseVariableFactor

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Pool identifier: `keccak256(xdr(PoolKey))`, the Soroban analogue of `PoolKey.toId`.

A compact 32-byte handle for a pool: pass it to `mint`/`burn`/`swap` (and the read
helpers) instead of re-supplying the full `PoolKey` on every call. Only `create_pool`,
`pool_id`, and `pool_exists` still take the full key.

A `#[contracttype]` newtype, NOT a bare `type` alias: an alias makes the spec macros emit
an undefined UDT named "PoolId" (the CLI then fails "Missing Entry PoolId" on
deploy/invoke), whereas the newtype registers a real spec entry. Being a 1-tuple, its wire
form wraps the inner bytes \xe2\x80\x94 the CLI renders a `PoolId` as `["<hex>"]` (like `Wad`), not a
bare `"<hex>"`. Reach the inner `BytesN<32>` via `.0`.
udt_struct_v0.name: PoolId

udt_struct_v0.doc: Trader / LP account. `isolated_margin_token = None` is unrestricted (cross) margin;\n`Some(token)` selects isolated-margin mode against that asset.
udt_struct_v0.name: Account

udt_struct_v0.doc: Pool identity passed to the CollateralEngine.
udt_struct_v0.name: PoolKey

udt_struct_v0.doc: Swap inputs. `amount_specified > 0` is a fixed taker (exact input), `< 0` a variable\ntaker (exact output). `tick_lower`/`tick_upper` identify the position for the engine.
udt_struct_v0.name: SwapParams

udt_struct_v0.doc: Swap outputs.
udt_struct_v0.name: SwapResult

fields.doc: How much of `amount_specified` the swap consumed, in the units it was given in. Equals it on\na full fill; short when the price limit stopped the loop or the pool ran out of liquidity.
fields.name: notional_filled

fields.doc: The position's variable balance change, in the pool's term-start-anchored tokens. Below\n`notional_filled` by the accrued factor whenever the trade lands mid-term, which is why a\ncaller checking "did I get the notional I asked for" must read `notional_filled` instead.
fields.name: variable_token_delta

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Arguments for `CollateralEngine.update_position_post_vamm_action`.

Mixed-width by design: the token deltas are SEP-41 `i128` amounts, while the
growth-inside fields are X128 per-unit-liquidity accumulators carried as host `I256`.
udt_struct_v0.name: UpdatePositionParams

fields.doc:
The VAMM's current sqrt price at the time of this action, passed so the engine can run the
LP worst-case sweep without calling back into the VAMM (which is on the call stack).

The price rather than the tick: an LP's balance is a function of where the price actually
rests, and the realized side the engine pairs this with already reflects that, so starting
the hypothetical sweep from a floored tick would leave the two describing different points.
fields.name: current_sqrt_price

udt_struct_v0.doc: An unsigned WAD (`1e18`) fixed-point quantity: a rate, fee, or duration in seconds.
udt_struct_v0.name: Wad

udt_struct_v0.doc: A `Q64.96` sqrt price (`sqrt(token1/token0) * 2^96`). The pool-constrained range\n(`tick_math::{MIN,MAX}_SQRT_PRICE`) fits in `u128`; wide intermediates widen via\n[`to_u256`](Self::to_u256).
udt_struct_v0.name: SqrtPriceX96

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A Unix timestamp in WAD-scaled seconds (`seconds * 1e18`), the EVM
`Time.blockTimestampScaled` convention. Distinct from [`Wad`] so a point in time is
never mistaken for a duration: timestamps only compare and subtract (yielding a
[`Wad`] duration).
udt_struct_v0.name: TimestampWad
